verses.restored: Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent to Samaria, to rulers of Jezreel, elders, and guardians of Ahab, saying,
Now when this letter comes to you, since sons of your master are with you, and chariots, horses, fortified city, and weapons are with you,
see the best and most upright of sons of your master, set him on throne of his father, and fight for house of your master.
They feared greatly and said, Look, two kings did not stand before him; how then shall we stand?
One over house, one over city, elders, and guardians sent to Jehu, saying, Your servants are we; all you say to us we will do. We will not make a man king; do what is good in your eyes.

He wrote to them a second letter, saying, If you are for me and listen to my voice, take heads of men, sons of your master, and come to me at Jezreel tomorrow at this time. King's sons, seventy men, were with great men of city who raised them.
When letter came to them, they took king's sons and slaughtered seventy men, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to him at Jezreel.
Messenger came and told him, They have brought heads of king's sons. He said, Set them in two heaps at entrance of gate until morning.
In morning he went out, stood, and said to all people, You are righteous. Look, I conspired against my master and killed him, but who struck all these?
Know therefore that nothing from word of YHWH shall fall to earth, which YHWH spoke against house of Ahab; YHWH has done what he spoke by hand of Elijah his servant.
Jehu struck all remaining from house of Ahab in Jezreel, all his great men, acquaintances, and priests, until he left him no survivor.
He rose, went, and came to Samaria. He was at Beth-eked of shepherds on way.
Jehu found brothers/relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, Who are you? They said, Brothers of Ahaziah are we, and we are going down for peace of sons of king and sons of queen mother.
He said, Seize them alive. They seized them alive and slaughtered them at pit of Beth-eked, forty-two men; he left no man from them.

He went from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He blessed him and said, Is your heart upright as my heart is with your heart? Jehonadab said, It is. If it is, give your hand. He gave his hand and brought him up into chariot.
He said, Come with me and see my zeal for YHWH. So they made him ride in his chariot.
He came to Samaria and struck all remaining to Ahab in Samaria until he destroyed him, according to word of YHWH spoken to Elijah.
Jehu gathered all people and said to them, Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.

Now call to me all prophets of Baal, all his servants, and all his priests; let no one be missing, for a great sacrifice I have for Baal. All who are missing shall not live. But Jehu acted with deception in order to destroy servants of Baal.
Jehu said, Sanctify a solemn assembly for Baal. They proclaimed it.
Jehu sent through all Israel, and all servants of Baal came; not a man remained who did not come. They entered house of Baal, and house of Baal was filled from mouth to mouth.
He said to one over wardrobe, Bring out garments for all servants of Baal. He brought out garments for them.
Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab came into house of Baal. He said to servants of Baal, Search and see lest there be here with you any from servants of YHWH, but servants of Baal alone.
They entered to make sacrifices and burnt offerings. Jehu had stationed eighty men outside and said, The man who lets escape any from men I bring into your hands—his soul/life for his soul/life.

When he finished making burnt offering, Jehu said to runners and officers, Go in, strike them; let no man go out. They struck them by edge of sword, runners and officers threw them out, and went as far as city/inner area of house of Baal.
They brought out pillars of house of Baal and burned them.
They tore down pillar of Baal, tore down house of Baal, and made it into latrines to this day.
Thus Jehu destroyed Baal from Israel.
Only from sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who caused Israel to sin, Jehu did not turn aside—from golden calves at Bethel and Dan.
YHWH said to Jehu, Because you did well in doing what is right in my eyes, according to all in my heart you did to house of Ahab, sons of fourth generation shall sit for you on throne of Israel.
But Jehu did not guard to walk in Torah of YHWH Divine of Israel with all his heart; he did not turn aside from sins of Jeroboam, who caused Israel to sin.
In those days YHWH began to cut off parts of Israel, and Hazael struck them in all border of Israel,
from Jordan toward sunrise: all land of Gilead, Gadites, Reubenites, Manassites, from Aroer by wadi Arnon, Gilead, and Bashan.
Remaining acts of Jehu, all he did, and all his might, are they not written in scroll of words of days of kings of Israel?
Jehu lay with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria. Jehoahaz his son became king in his place.
Days Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria were twenty-eight years.

translation_notes: Jehu coerces officials and guardians into killing seventy royal sons. Their fear, complicity, and the children's dependence on elite protectors remain visible.
The severed heads are displayed at the city gate as political terror. Public spectacle does not become justice because it is linked to prophecy.
Jehu rhetorically spreads guilt—'who struck all these?'—while he designed the coercive order. Leaders remain responsible for violence they induce others to carry out.
Ahaziah's forty-two relatives are seized and slaughtered despite no narrated trial or individual wrongdoing.
Jehu's alliance with Jehonadab validates his zeal politically, but zeal is not an ethical substitute for evidence, due process, or protection of life.
The Baal assembly is created through deception, compulsory attendance, identity sorting, armed encirclement, and mass execution. It is religious persecution and massacre.
Distinctive garments become targeting markers. Religious clothing, affiliation, or attendance may never be used to identify people for harm.
The destruction and conversion of Baal's temple into latrines is humiliation of a religious community, not a modern reform model.
The narrator both credits Jehu's destruction of Ahab and criticizes his incomplete covenant loyalty, exposing the moral and theological instability of his reign.
Hazael's territorial victories show Jehu's violence did not produce secure or just peace.
safety_note: Do not use 2 Kings 10 to justify child killing, dynastic purges, severed-head displays, coercive orders, religious deception, forced registration, targeting by clothing, massacre of worshippers, destruction of sacred sites, or leader claims that zeal excuses atrocity. This chapter is a warning about reform becoming terror.
